title: Low water
summary: Third dry August in four years. The archive is trying not to draw a conclusion from this and is not managing it.
weather: Clear, 24 °C, no cloud in any direction

body.text: The tide line — which is not a tide line, but there is no better word for it — is about four metres below the tree line, and between the two there is a band of pale silt, cracked into plates roughly the size of a hand.

Things in the exposed ground, in order of appearance: a gatepost. A quantity of barbed wire. Two horseshoes. The road. A traffic cone, which had clearly been thrown in and was not of historical interest but has been noted anyway in the interest of an honest record.
The exposure is entertaining and the reason for the exposure is not. Both are true at once and the archive has no plan for reconciling them.
